Tracked armour of the later Ages: heavy battle-chariots of iron, two designs in three marks and three paints. A driver sits in the hull, the commander and gunner under the turret; the gun turns all the way round.
Main Battle Tank Mk I: Early heavy tracked armour with a 105 mm gun. Crew of two or more; built at the vehicle bench from iron, redstone and gunpowder. Forest, desert and winter paint.
Main Battle Tank Mk IA: Mk I with the 120 mm gun and a thicker front. Crew of two or more; built at the vehicle bench from iron, redstone and gunpowder. Forest, desert and winter paint.
Main Battle Tank Mk IB: Mk IA with composite side skirts and a stronger engine. Crew of two or more; built at the vehicle bench from iron, redstone and gunpowder. Forest, desert and winter paint.
Main Battle Tank Mk II: Low, domed three-crew tank with an autoloaded 125 mm gun. Crew of two or more; built at the vehicle bench from iron, redstone and gunpowder. Forest, desert and winter paint.
Main Battle Tank Mk IIA: Mk II with added turret armour and smoke launchers. Crew of two or more; built at the vehicle bench from iron, redstone and gunpowder. Forest, desert and winter paint.
Main Battle Tank Mk IIB: Mk IIA with composite armour and a stronger engine. Crew of two or more; built at the vehicle bench from iron, redstone and gunpowder. Forest, desert and winter paint.
